detailed_source_maps.analytic_sources.txt:
ANALYTIC PROOF: SOURCE AND VERIFICATION MAP

Primary mathematical source:
Aabir Fauzan, "zeta(5) is irrational", manuscript 17 September 2026,
https://zenodo.org/records/22826419
Local sources/Fauzan_2026_zeta5.pdf and .txt.
Section6: comparison external field, zero-mass energy, smoothing,
configuration bound, scaling and normalization.
AppendixA Tables1-2: all sixteen rational arcsine components and complete
684-interval partition. EquationsA.1-A.10: potentials, energy and
elementary series certificate.

Formal source used as cross-check:
Moritz Firsching, Zeta5 Lean project,
https://github.com/mo271/Zeta5
Fixed revision 7fe736760f4b96bfdb4334b68e3b3124ecbe10b0.
Apache-2.0. The repository's license is preserved in the source checkout.

Exact files/declarations consulted:
Apery/Measure.lean: table1, a/b/c data, M0, Cstar, Irho.
Apery/Andreief.lean and Apery/DetIntegral.lean: determinant integral.
Apery/Energy.lean: w_le', integral_le_sum_log, sum_log_le_integral.
Apery/RealBound.lean: log_Δ_le, log_S_le, real_bound'.
Apery/EnergyConst.lean: log_ge_artanh, log_ge_of_pow_two, energy_const.
Apery/ArcsinePotential.lean: arcsine potential and continuity.
Apery/Gaussian.lean, ZeroMass.lean, EnergyLimit.lean,
EnergyFinal.lean: decomposition described in the repository README.
Apery/TableCheck.lean and Apery/Table/: finite potential certificate.
scripts/lemma61.py: literal transcription of Table1 and compressed Table2.
scripts/gen_table2.py: comparison of certificate design; not executed.

Relation to the new prose:
The construction, constants, measure, partition, and proof strategy are
Fauzan's. The added text expands elementary proofs and checks the
arithmetic operations, integrability and scaling. No claim of a new
analytic method is made. Firsching's formalization is explicitly credited
for the detailed implementation and safe final bound with coefficient27.
The prose uses an elementary upper error7h for log S, rather than source6h;
this harmless relaxation is derived directly.

Verification supplied with this draft:
analytic_data.json is transcribed from the data in scripts/lemma61.py,
with attribution and SHA256 of the source file. The numerical sampling
in that source script is NOT used.
analytic_certificate.py is a new standard-library implementation of exact
outward interval arithmetic on a dyadic grid2^-112; it encloses logarithms
and arctangents using proved series tails, and square roots using isqrt.
It checks nesting, masses, minimum-location signs, exact partition
coverage, all684 interval bounds, the tail at2, and the energy constant.
analytic_certificate.json contains its exact rational result and hashes.
analytic_intervals.csv lists every interval and its exact bound.
No Lean build was run by the analytic author; references to formalization
are source comparisons, not a claim of a new independent kernel build.

Important distinction:
M0=-1329/200=-6.645.
The finite interval target is -6645002/1000000=-6.645002, strictly smaller.
The energy constant always uses M0, not the stricter interval target.

Classical mathematical facts proved in the prose:
Andréief determinant identity; circle mean-log identity; arcsine
potential via factorization; logarithm/arctangent series bounds;
Gaussian proof of zero-mass energy; local arcsine mass estimate;
factorial and Riemann-sum comparisons. Routine Fubini/Tonelli/dominated
convergence are stated with the required integrability checks.
detailed_source_maps.local_sources.txt:
LOCAL ARITHMETIC SOURCE MAP
Prepared 14 November 2026.

Principal source snapshot:
  Moritz Firsching, mo271/Zeta5, commit
  7fe736760f4b96bfdb4334b68e3b3124ecbe10b0.
  Local checkout: sources/mo271-Zeta5.
  Base URL:
  https://github.com/mo271/Zeta5/blob/7fe736760f4b96bfdb4334b68e3b3124ecbe10b0/
  Source is Apache-2.0. No source code is reproduced in the exposition;
  the mathematical constructions and proofs are translated into prose.
  This text does not claim an independently rebuilt Lean proof.

Earlier principal source:
  Aabir Fauzan, zeta(5) is irrational, 17 September 2026.
  https://zenodo.org/records/22826419
  Local PDF/text: sources/Fauzan_2026_zeta5.pdf / .txt.
  Original sections 3--4 provide tau, pullback, integer-valued basis,
  residue-class bases, weights, and the three-range organization.

Mapping to local_arithmetic.tex:

1. Gauss valuations and weighted determinants:
   Apery/Arith/Val.lean, det_GV;
   Apery/Arith/BasisChange.lean, det_basis_change.
   Standard permutation expansion and bilinear basis change.

2. tau, pole extension and pullback:
   Fauzan section 3, equation (3.1).
   Apery/Arith/PoleFun.lean, tauX, dd;
   Apery/Arith/Pullback.lean, muX_eq_tauX.
   The full pullback proof is retained in the root appendix.

3. Integer-valued polynomial estimate:
   Fauzan equation (3.9).
   Apery/Arith/BinomBasis.lean;
   Apery/Arith/TauBound.lean, tau_bound;
   Apery/Arith/SmallPrime.lean, VG_eval_int_of_window.
   The exposition derives the binomial identities from formal generating
   functions and gives the valuation proof.

4. Coarse rational-function estimate:
   Apery/Arith/SmallPrimeTau.lean, crude_tauX.
   Direct integer-window proof with residues at +/-1,...,+/-K;
   it replaces the original analytic-ball argument.
   The factorial ratio and elementary binomial valuation bound are shown.

5. Coarse bound on F:
   Fauzan (3.11)--(3.12).
   Apery/Arith/SmallPrimeF.lean, small_prime_bound.
   Exact q_i basis, integral evaluations, determinant normalization.

6. Direct residue-class lemma including polynomial parts:
   Apery/Arith/DirectBound.lean, VG_res;
   Apery/Arith/DirectPoly.lean, VG_polyPart_eval, tauX_direct.
   The substitution x=m+pz and monic-division argument are reproduced
   mathematically, not replaced by a code citation.

7. Inner CRT basis and capped row weights:
   Fauzan section 4.1.
   Apery/Arith/ClassFrame.lean, class_frame;
   Apery/Arith/ClassCount.lean, Bse;
   Apery/Arith/InnerWeights.lean, inner_bound_cap.
   Zero count has the additional 5 from x^5; s_H(0) is doubled.

8. Water-filling allocation:
   Apery/Arith/InnerAlloc.lean, kfSel, PhiK_le_kf.
   Apery/Norm.lean, betaI, kloI, ktopI, L0I, allocI.
   The exposition proves the uniform O_400(1) version used by the
   growth section, instead of carrying the formal source's large
   explicit auxiliary constants. No change in the chosen allocation.

9. Outer basis and nonpositive weights:
   Fauzan section 4.2.
   Apery/Arith/OuterBasis.lean, rootsO;
   Apery/Arith/OuterEntryMain.lean, wO, outer_entry, outer_bound.
   The exposition writes the root multisets as polynomial products.

10. Pole congruence and two-pole cancellation:
    Apery/Arith/PoleVal.lean, GV_poleValue_congr;
    Apery/Arith/OuterEntries.lean, pair_GV;
    Apery/Arith/OuterEntryMain.lean, pole_case_a, pole_case_b,
    pole_case_zero.
    Harmonic congruence, divided differences and both zero-class cases
    are explained explicitly.

11. Bernoulli high-moment correction and rank loss:
    Apery/Arith/MomentVal.lean, VG_muMono_int;
    Apery/Arith/OuterFrame.lean, outer_frame;
    Apery/Arith/LowRank.lean, det_lowrank_bound.
    Uses the standard von Staudt--Clausen theorem, stated in text.
    Full loss r=max(0,52n+2-2p), NOT the original min(r,z).
    Block determinant proof is included.

12. Uniform conditions:
    Sufficient conservative threshold K>480000, n>=12001.
    Then p>K/400 implies p^2>3K, stronger than the source's listed
    separation and degree conditions. Only eventual bounds are needed.

Coverage:
  All new argument-specific local inequalities are proved in prose.
  Standard facts used: finite-difference interpolation, elementary
  arithmetic of valuations, Chinese remainder theorem, Legendre's
  factorial valuation formula, von Staudt--Clausen, determinant identities.
  The source-dependent choices of bases, weights and allocation are
  explicitly credited. Finite checks are supplementary and do not
  substitute for the general proofs.

PARALLEL-CONSTRUCTIONS REVISION: EXPLANATORY PROVENANCE
14 November 2026

Requested chat:
  Find parallel constructions in the Zeta(5)...
  App title uses a final ellipsis character.
  Thread ID: 01a1dc1f-f2bf-7531-976e-7f07e6a19ab0
  All four turns retrieved through read_thread; hasMore=false.
  The final provenance correction controls the earlier novelty wording.

Corrected companion:
  ../zeta5_unified_framework.tex (relative to the document folder)
  SHA256:
  aa4d266a6cd21ec515e5290ad1a5f2a3b8734e842e00fcd3ee4ae10c59c91f72

What was incorporated:
  * One bilinear form, viewed through its positive integral and residue
    slope; this removes a repeated residue calculation in the degree proof.
    Underlying source: Fauzan Sections 2.3-2.4.
  * Primitive evaluation size, invariant under rational scaling.
    Underlying source: Fauzan Appendix C.3; notation/teaching emphasis
    from the chat.
  * Three arithmetic coordinate choices: integer values, prescribed
    residue-class vanishing, and exact cancellation of pole factors.
    Underlying strategy: Fauzan Sections 3-4; the implementation remains
    Firsching's revised finite partial-fraction argument.
  * Polynomial Euler-Maclaurin operator, interpreted as a terminating
    formal series. Classical input: DLMF 24.2 and 24.4.
    No p-adic analytic extension is assumed.
  * Finite products/counts versus their continuous logarithmic/arithmetic
    profiles. Underlying estimates: Fauzan Sections 5-6, with Firsching's
    revised arithmetic profiles.
  * Equal-mass energy identity and distinct moment/configuration/comparison
    measures. Underlying source: Fauzan Section 6.1; the circle errors
    and finite potential certificate remain fully included.
  * Periodic Bernoulli descriptions of the existing tail primitives.
    Underlying integration argument: Fauzan Section 5.3 and Firsching
    Growth/TailIntegral.lean. DLMF 24.2-24.4 supplies classical notation.

What was shortened:
  The optional Pade-approximant error proof was condensed to the exact
  Stieltjes samples and finite moment remainder needed for the perspective.
  The exact-degree proof now uses the already established residue pairing.
  Duplicate determinant expansions and explanatory passages were trimmed.

Quantitative boundary:
  No original min(rank,zero-weight-count) saving or M=200 estimate was
  imported. The capped inner weights, full rank loss, M=400 arithmetic,
  comparison-measure data, and finite certificate inputs are unchanged.
  The chat is an expository source, not a new primary mathematical source.
